title: No AI After Auschwitz? Bridging AI and Memory Ethics in the Context of Information Retrieval of Genocide-Related Information
findings: The paper argues that AI-driven information retrieval systems pose significant ethical challenges when curating information about genocides with religious dimensions, such as the Holocaust (Judaism) and the Rohingya persecution (Islam). It finds that commercial platforms' algorithms can lead to unequal representation of historical events, promote denialist content, or suppress resistance to ideologies like antisemitism. The paper proposes bridging memory ethics with AI system design to address issues of consent, privacy, representation, and justice in this sensitive context.
